problem: Embodied AI evaluation is fragmented: benchmarks differ in data formats, metrics and target capabilities, so cross-benchmark comparison is infeasible; there is also no systematic capability taxonomy and no scalable automated way to produce embodied evaluation data.
motivation: Embodied AI lags behind foundation models partly because researchers lack clear capability objectives, a unified evaluation system, and scalable data. A single platform that unifies benchmarks under one capability taxonomy and keeps generating new data could expose model strengths and weaknesses and guide research directions.
key_idea: Build a unified, evolving evaluation platform (Embodied Arena) with a 3-level/7-capability/25-dimension taxonomy, a standardized infrastructure integrating 22 benchmarks and 30+ models, and an LLM-driven simulator-based data generation pipeline, publishing leaderboards in benchmark and capability views.
insight: Cross-benchmark leaderboards show that rankings fluctuate strongly across benchmarks (e.g. RoboBrain-7B is top on RoboVQA but poor on Where2Place/VSI-Bench), indicating benchmark-specific overfitting. Embodied capabilities correlate strongly with downstream performance only when general models are wrapped in task-oriented agentic frameworks (rho=0.79) versus end-to-end use (rho=0.40, not significant); general models get 5.80% navigation SR end-to-end versus 36.21% with agentic frameworks. Object and spatial perception are the bottlenecks, and no clear scaling law with model size or data has emerged for embodied models.
method: Capability taxonomy: three levels (perception, reasoning, task execution), 7 core capabilities (object, spatial, temporal perception, embodied knowledge, embodied reasoning, embodied navigation, embodied task planning) and 25 fine-grained dimensions; existing benchmarks are mapped onto it.

Unified evaluation system: standardized input/output formats, API / parameter / custom-interface model integration, experiment tracking; covers 22 benchmarks (2D/3D Embodied QA, Navigation: MP3D, HM3D, EB-Navigation, R2R-CE, RxR-CE; Task Planning: EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat, ET-Plan-Bench) and 30+ models (64k+ task instances).

Scoring rules: per-dimension accuracy averaged into benchmark scores; capability leaderboards map original benchmark dimensions to taxonomy dimensions and aggregate per dimension by pooled correct/total counts.

Automated scenario generation: LLM/VLM-guided hierarchical multi-room scene building (floor planning, functional zoning, layout planning) with high-fidelity rendering, domain randomization and a targeted-scene mode.

Capability-oriented data generation: simulator-driven procedural pipelines using privileged simulator annotations, automated filtering plus sampling-based human inspection, and a difficulty ladder over scene, language and task complexity.
Data evolution: periodically analyze model weaknesses and generate targeted new data; leaderboards updated monthly in benchmark and capability views.

setting.backbone: Evaluation platform; no single model (evaluates 30+ general MLLMs such as GPT-o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Qwen2.5-VL, InternVL3, and embodied models such as StreamVLN, NaVILA, UniNavid, RoboBrain2.0)
setting.observation: varies by benchmark: 2D images/video, 3D scans, egocentric RGB for navigation
setting.action_space: varies: text answers, discrete/low-level navigation actions, high-level task-planning action sequences
setting.simulator: Habitat (navigation, EB-Habitat), EmbodiedBench simulators, plus a generative simulator pipeline for data
setting.privileged: none for evaluated models; the data generation pipeline uses simulator privileged ground truth to create annotations

numbers_note: Platform/leaderboard paper with no own-method results. Model results are only cited in the findings text (e.g. StreamVLN 54.90%, NaVILA 51.65%, UniNavid 47.85% navigation SR) and leaderboard screenshots, which are baselines, not the paper's own method.
results: Across 30+ models and 22 benchmarks, nine findings emerge: embodied models beat similarly sized general models on specialized benchmarks, while large closed models (o3, Gemini-2.5-Pro) lead overall by 10-20%. VLN-specialized models (StreamVLN 54.90% SR) far outperform general models (Gemini-2.5-Pro 27.37%, GPT-4o 21.67%) in end-to-end navigation; benchmark overfitting and the absence of a scaling law are also reported.
limitations: Currently lacks direct simulation-based manipulation and closed-loop perception-decision-action evaluation.

Automated data generation still requires human sampling inspection, and generated data is not yet shown quantitatively in the paper; findings rely on leaderboard screenshots and correlations without detailed tables.
Navigation coverage is limited to a few benchmarks with mostly one-submission-per-month, and comparisons mix end-to-end and agentic frameworks.
